title: Building and Packaging Kotlin Applications
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of building and packaging kotlin applications using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates building and packaging kotlin applications.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Building and Packaging Kotlin Applications** as part of **Packages, Modules, Dependencies, and Build Tools**. Build reproducibility depends on the Gradle Wrapper, compatible plugin/toolchain versions, declared dependency scopes, and repeatable test/build commands. Use the subtopics—Compiling and Testing with Gradle, Creating Executable Artifacts, Runtime Dependency Packaging—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Real projects depend on reliable error handling, modular organization, reproducible builds, and safe language boundaries. This lesson helps turn isolated syntax into maintainable applications.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Build reproducibility depends on the Gradle Wrapper, compatible plugin/toolchain versions, declared dependency scopes, and repeatable test/build commands.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with compiling and testing with gradle. Then compare it with creating executable artifacts. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Compiling and Testing with Gradle
items.text: Compiling and Testing with Gradle helps make behavior observable and repeatable. Define the expected result, include a boundary or failure case, and preserve enough diagnostic information to locate the cause without leaking sensitive data.

items.title: Creating Executable Artifacts
items.text: Creating Executable Artifacts is one part of building and packaging kotlin applications. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Runtime Dependency Packaging
items.text: Runtime Dependency Packaging means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

content_blocks.expected_output: The build declares the Kotlin/JVM plugin, a repository, and Kotlin test dependency (configuration example).
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet in a Kotlin/JVM console project and run the configured Gradle application task, or use the Kotlin Playground for examples that need no external dependencies.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Building and Packaging Kotlin Applications removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

items.title: Explain
items.text: Describe the main rule of building and packaging kotlin applications in your own words.

items.title: Apply
items.text: Change one input or condition and predict the result before running it.

items.title: Verify
items.text: Check one edge case and the official reference for the selected Kotlin/runtime version.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates building and packaging kotlin applications. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving compiling and testing with gradle.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain building and packaging kotlin applications without copying the lesson wording.

Compare your observed result with the expected output and the official reference; verify that you are using the required project type and dependency set.
